title: Genetic programs for complex pigment patterns are short

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Genetic programs for complex pigment patterns are short

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The genetic programs that generate patterns such as those on mollusc shells are short, as indicated by the large variety of patterns within species, and molecular biology should be able to isolate them and confirm their brevity.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Modern molecular biology should soon be able to isolate the specific programs responsible, say, for the patterns on mollusc shells, and see explicitly how long they are. But there are already indications that these programs are quite short.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 8, “Implications for Everyday Systems”; section “Fundamental Issues in Biology” (from p. 383), p. 390. Scope: genetic control of pigmentation patterns, especially on mollusc shells

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch08-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.50

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public mollusc genomes and transcriptomes can identify candidate pigmentation components in some species. Demonstrating a complete minimal program normally requires perturbation and developmental data that are uneven or absent. Existing data can estimate program size only for selected systems.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Identify cis-regulatory and coding loci causally required for shell pigmentation through expression, perturbation, and segregation evidence, then measure the minimal sequence and regulatory-network description sufficient to recreate pattern classes. Long indispensable programs or highly distributed control would refute the brevity claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Sequence association does not identify the complete causal program.

Functional genomic coverage of shell-pattern diversity is sparse.

Short lacks an explicit unit and threshold.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.32
analysis feasibility: 0.48
data existence: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.62
discriminating power: 0.52

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Program length is a measurable quantity once the responsible regulatory program is identified, so the prediction is testable in principle. Public genomes and taxonomic catalogs do not contain those programs or their lengths, and the diversity proxy does not decide brevity. Resolving the claim requires data that have not been collected.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Identify the gene-regulatory elements that control shell pigmentation and measure their functional length, then test whether that length is short relative to a pre-registered baseline. Within-species pattern variety is only a proxy: high variety together with a short mapped program would support the claim, while a long program would refute it even if patterns vary.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Pattern variety can come from many polymorphic loci in a long program, so diversity does not measure length.

The pigmentation programs for shell patterns have not been isolated for a representative set of species.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.3
operationalizability: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.35
analysis feasibility: 0.3
data adequacy: 0.25
